name: Snark News Toon
description: Today's headlines, reported accurately and then punctured — a 60-second satirical newscast.

config.userPrompt:
From the RSS below, pick the THREE stories that are both NEWSWORTHY and can carry
irony — institutions behaving absurdly, industries contradicting themselves, official
nonsense. EXCLUDE anything whose subject is a death, an injury, a missing person, a crime
against a person, or an obituary: those are reported straight or not at all, never joked
about. Return ONLY the article URLs, one per line, nothing else.

{{INPUT}}

Write a SIXTY SECOND satirical news bulletin for a two-anchor cartoon newsdesk.

ANCHORS: DALE, lead anchor, unshakeable broadcast voice, treats the absurd as routine.
         PRIYA, co-anchor, drier, lands the ironic observation.

RULES
- About 150 words. Sixty seconds read aloud.
- Cover the three stories below, in order, three or four exchanges each.
- THE NEWS MUST STILL LAND. Every story gets its actual facts FIRST — the number, the
  place, the decision — and the wry line comes after. A viewer who watches this should
  come away genuinely informed. A joke that replaces the fact has failed.
- Aim the irony at institutions, industries and absurd situations. NEVER at individuals
  suffering, NEVER at anyone's death or injury.
- Anchors trade lines. Nobody makes a speech.
- Open with a greeting, close with a sign-off.
- Plain spoken lines only. NO stage directions, NO parentheses, NO camera notes —
  anything in brackets gets read aloud by the voice engine.

OUTPUT EXACTLY THIS SHAPE AND NOTHING ELSE:
DALE: <line>
PRIYA: <line>

SOURCE MATERIAL:
{{INPUT}}

Turn this news bulletin into the STUDIO GRAPHICS behind the anchors.

WHAT THESE ARE. Not slides to read. Each card is the over-shoulder graphic a real
newsroom puts up while a story is being read: one story, one card, understood in two
seconds from across a room, at a third of screen width, behind a cartoon anchor's head.

THE RULE THAT DECIDES WHETHER THIS WORKS. Every card must use the words the anchors
actually SAY about that story — the name, the place, the organisation. That is what pairs
the card with the moment it goes up. A card whose words appear nowhere in the script
cannot be placed and gets dropped.

CHOOSING THE CARD, in this order:
1. If the story turns on a NUMBER, make it a "bigFact": the number alone, huge, with a
   short label under it.
2. If it turns on something someone SAID, make it a "quote".
3. Otherwise make it a "title": the headline, and one line under it.

Never invent a number, a name or a quote. Only what the bulletin says. One card per
story, in the order the bulletin covers them. No opening card, no sign-off card.

LENGTH. `fact` is at most 8 characters ("£2.4bn", "15%", "50ft"). Every `label`,
`title` and `subtitle` is six words at most; three is better.

OUTPUT RAW JSON, no fence, no commentary:

{"slides":[
  {"layout":"bigFact","fact":"50ft","label":"Between two passenger jets","caption":"Airlink"},
  {"layout":"title","title":"Met cancels Galliano show","subtitle":"After sustained backlash"},
  {"layout":"quote","quote":"Nothing says enjoy the game like a near miss","attribution":"Priya"}
]}
